Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru.Prin.Secy.Home And Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Vishnu Kumar Srivastava,Devendra Kumar Pathak
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajai Kumar Srivastava-I,J.
1.

At the outset, learned counsel for the applicants has stated that he does not want to press the instant application in respect to applicant no.1 and the same may be dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to file a fresh application with better particulars in respect to the applicant no.1.
2. Learned A.G.A. for the State has no objection to the aforesaid prayer.

3. Accordingly, the instant application is dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to file a fresh application with better particulars in respect to the applicant no.1.
4.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the entire record.

5. This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants for quashing the charge sheet no.330 of 2022 dated 14.11.2022, under Sections 354-A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. in F.I.R.

1 No.0223 of 2022, Police Station Jethwara, District Pratapgarh filed against the applicants and also quashing the summoning order dated 08.02.2023 issued against the applicant no.1 under Sections 376, 354A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. as well as against the applicant nos.2 and 3 under Sections 323, 504,
506 I.P.C. by Upper Civil Judge, (Junior Division)/Judicial Magistrate, Room No.15, Pratapgarh as well as quashing the entire proceedings of Case No.0223 of 2022 "State vs. Vakeel Ahamad" in pursuance of charge sheet no.330 of 2022, Police Station Jethwara, District Pratapgarh, pending in the Court of learned Upper Civil Judge (Junior Division)/Judicial Magistrate, Room No.15,
Pratapgarh.
6.
Learned counsel for the applicant nos.2 and 3 has submitted that accused/ applicant nos.2 and 3 are innocent, who have been falsely implicated in this case due to some ulterior reason.
7. His further submission is that the content of the first information report does not disclose any ingredients, which are essential to constitute offence under Sections 354-A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C.
He has also submitted that even during investigation, no credible evidence could be collected against the present accused/ applicant nos.2 and 3.

Despite this fact, a charge sheet came to be laid mechanically against the applicant nos.2 and 3.
8.
His next submission is that the learned trial court, vide order dated 08.02.2023, proceeded to take cognizance and consequently, the applicant nos.2 and 3 came to be summoned to stand trial.

9. Learned counsel for the applicant nos.2 and 3, on the basis of aforesaid submissions, has submitted that the present proceeding is nothing but an abuse of process of this Court and a malicious prosecution too, which deserves to be quashed.

10. Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State has vehemently submitted that the law of quashing has been fairly settled in the celebrated judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Haryana vs. Bhajan Lal reported in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 and R.P. Kapur Vs. State of Punjab AIR 1960 SC 866.
11.

sentences.text: His further submission is that in view of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramveer Upadhyay vs. State of U.P. reported in AIR 2022 SC 2044 and Rathish Babu Unnikrishnan vs. State (NCT of Delhi) reported in 2022 SCC OnLine SC 513, truthfulness or otherwise of the prosecution version or defence version cannot be looked into at this stage.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Rathish Babu Unnikrishnan vs. State (NCT of Delhi) reported in 2022 SCC OnLine SC 513
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At such an early stage to rush of this Court for quashing itself is an abuse of process of this Court as the trial has not progressed substantially.
12. Thus, in view of aforesaid, learned A.G.A. has submitted that the present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is devoid of merit and deserves to be dismissed.

13. Having heard the learned counsel for the applicant nos.2 and 3, learned A.G.A. for the State and upon perusal of record including the first information report and the charge sheet laid against the present applicant, this Court is of considered view that in view of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bhajan Lal's case (supra), R.P. Kapur's case (supra), Ramveer Upadhyay's case Vakeel Ahamad And Others vs State Of U.P. Thru.Prin.Secy.Home And ... on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4038518/
2 (supra) and Rathish Babu Unnikrishnan's case (supra), no ground for quashing the instant proceeding exists.
14.

entities.text: Vakeel Ahamad And Others vs State Of U.P. Thru.Prin.Secy.Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the prayer for quashing the entire proceeding of aforesaid case, the impugned charge sheet as well as impugned summoning order is refused as this Court does not find any illegality, impropriety and incorrectness in the proceedings under challenge.
There is no abuse of court's process either.

15. Even otherwise, the applicant nos.2 and 3 will have an opportunity at the appropriate stage to move an application for discharge taking therein all the pleas factual and legal which may be available to them, in accordance with law.
In case, such an application is moved before the learned trial Court, the learned trial Court shall dispose of the same by a speaking and reasoned order strictly, in accordance with law.

16. However, it is needless to mention that if the applicant nos.2 and 3 apply for grant of bail, the court below shall consider and decide the same expeditiously, in accordance with law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antill vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and others : MANU/SC/1024/2021.
17.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antill vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and others : MANU/SC/1024/2021.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With the aforesaid observations, the instant application is finally disposed of.
